# Pets & Animals — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Pets: typically around 1,750, most listings 450–4,500 (14 listings).

Data is thin (n=14) and skews to birds and small pets (budgies, pigeons, hamsters, rabbits). Pedigree dogs and cats legitimately sell for NPR 10,000–60,000+, so a price above p90 is NOT suspicious here — judge by species/breed. The scam signal is the reverse: a known expensive breed priced far below its normal market (e.g. a "Husky puppy" at NPR 2,000) -> hold.

## What good listings look like
- "hand tamed female budgie"
- "Lakka pegions"
- "lovebirds"
- "Hamster and hamster cage"
- "Optimum 100gm Highly Nutritious Fish Food For Aquariumn Fish"

A good listing names the species or breed plus a key attribute (tamed, sex, age, included cage/supplies); pet supplies name brand and size.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Pedigree/imported breeds at far-below-market prices, especially with "delivery from another city" or advance-booking/deposit terms — the classic Nepal puppy-scam pattern -> hold.
- Free or token-price "adoption" ads that ask for a transport fee or advance payment before handover -> hold.
- This category has zero editor rejections on record — do not invent extra strictness beyond the above.
